To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a/A dilution is an index of regional pulmonary blood flow.

the inert gas method for the continuous measurement of regional pulmonary blood flow (regional Qc) is virtually independent of changes in pulmonary O2 and CO2, and that this method can be used with inert gases of very low solubility and normal alveolar/capillary (A/c) differences.

the inert gas method is a reliable and practical method for regional blood flow measurement in one lung compartment and that the a/A dilution method can be used to measure regional blood flow in the normal lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method of continuous measurement of regional pulmonary blood flow, which will be applicable in the intact human subject.

a method of regional pulmonary blood flow determination in which the labelling gas is a physiologically inert gas, and the dilution of this gas in systemic arterial (and hence mixed venous) blood is used to calculate the regional flow.
the development and evaluation of a method for the measurement of regional pulmonary blood flow (regional Qc) in man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inert gas method is theoretically feasible and that it can be used to measure regional blood flow in a lung compartment with minimal disturbance of the pulmonary circulation.
the theory of an inert gas technique for regional pulmonary blood flows is a valid and reliable one.
the method is theoretically sound, and that its practical application is feasible with inert gases of low blood/gas partition coefficients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method is simple and accurate, and that the choice of the labelling gas is critical.
a/A dilution is a direct measure of regional Qc/c and that this is the most important result to be derived from our work.

the theory of an inert gas technique for measuring regional pulmonary blood flow can be developed in a manner that makes it virtually independent of pulmonary O2 and CO2, and that the technique is capable of measuring regional pulmonary blood flows of 1-2 ml/min/100 ml of lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of inert gases for the measurement of regional blood flow in one compartment is feasible and is independent of pulmonary O2 and CO2 concentration.
the A/a dilution method can be used to measure regional blood flow in the lung, and that it is virtually insensitive to changes in pulmonary o2 or CO2 concentrations.
the use of a single inert gas for regional blood flow measurements is feasible and has a number of potential advantages.
